howTo.title: Step by step
steps: Drop all the footage of your shoot into AutoTrim: video or audio-only files, from one camera or several.
Choose what to remove: silences, hesitations (“um”, “uh”), or both. Adjust the threshold if you want more breathing room.
Play the preview to hear what was removed. Processing and previewing are free.
Export the timeline for Final Cut Pro (FCPXML), then in Final Cut Pro choose File > Import > XML.
Edit as usual. Each cut is a regular edit on your original files: drag a clip edge to bring a breath back.

0.q: How do I remove silences in Final Cut Pro automatically?
0.a: Final Cut Pro can't do it on its own, so you clean the footage first. Drop all your clips into AutoTrim, let it remove the silences and hesitations on your machine, check the preview, then export an FCPXML timeline and import it in Final Cut Pro (File > Import > XML). Every cut stays adjustable.

1.q: Does Final Cut Pro have a built-in silence remover?
1.a: No. As of October 2026, Final Cut Pro has no built-in command that detects and removes silences. You either cut each pause with the Blade tool or use a separate tool such as AutoTrim, which gives you back an FCPXML timeline.

2.q: Can Final Cut Pro remove filler words like “um” and “uh”?
2.a: Not automatically. AutoTrim removes hesitations in about ten languages, including English and French, along with the silences. You can listen to each removed hesitation in the preview before exporting.

3.q: Is AutoTrim a Final Cut Pro plugin?
3.a: No. AutoTrim is a standalone app for Mac and Windows that works before Final Cut Pro: it processes the whole shoot at once and exports an FCPXML timeline. A few third-party effects detect silence inside Final Cut Pro; AutoTrim also removes hesitations, syncs multicam takes and assembles every clip into one timeline.

4.q: Can I still adjust the cuts in Final Cut Pro?
4.a: Yes. The timeline is made of regular edits on your original files, which stay intact. Drag the edge of a clip to bring a breath back or tighten a cut.

5.q: Does it work with multicam shoots and a separate audio recorder?
5.a: Yes. AutoTrim finds the files that belong to the same take (several cameras, a separate audio recorder), syncs them, and only cuts when nobody is speaking.

6.a: No. All the processing runs on your machine. Nothing is uploaded.

7.a: Free to try, with unlimited previews. Exporting needs a license: $19/month, $149/year or $249 lifetime (one-time payment). Each license works on 2 computers, and there is a 14-day money-back guarantee.

8.q: How much editing time does it save?
8.a: It depends on how much silence your footage has. Across about 2,500 hours of footage processed by AutoTrim, the median share of silence was one third. James, a Final Cut editor, saves “at least one to two hours on a typical project”.

details.mic: AutoTrim cuts when nobody speaks. One guest’s um stays if someone else is speaking at the same time. Listen to each mic on its own to check.
details.follow: Match the cameras to the speakers: the preview switches to whoever is talking, or to the wide shot when voices overlap.

items.q: Final Cut Pro, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve?
items.a: Yes: FCPXML for Final Cut Pro and Resolve, XML for Premiere Pro. One timeline, all your files end to end, every clip with its handles.

items.q: Do my files leave my computer?
items.a: No, never. The models download once, then everything happens on your machine, even offline.

items.q: What if it cuts too much?
items.a: The preview shows three states, kept, silence, hesitation, and you can listen to what was removed. Adjust the threshold, run again, then export: every cut stays editable in your editing software.

items.q: My podcast has one mic per person?
items.a: Yes. AutoTrim only cuts when nobody speaks, never two voices at once, and one person's "um" only goes if the other is silent.

AutoTrim combines sound, durations and recording metadata to find files from the same take. Shared sound lets it measure offsets and clock drift between devices. Without shared sound, as with isolated Riverside tracks, matching start times and durations can also bring the files together. The app flags groups that need checking; you can view the angles in a mosaic, listen to each mic and adjust the sync. The preview can follow the speaker, and export keeps angles and mics on separate tracks, synced and cut together.

items.q: Which languages are hesitations detected in?
items.a: About ten languages, including English and French. Silences have no language.

items.q: Screen recordings (OBS, VLC, QuickTime), variable frame rate?
items.a: Supported. The real duration is kept, so the timeline lands right.
Take the video already cut, one MP4 per source. For CapCut, one numbered clip per cut, to drop in order.
Yes, same processing. Export as AAC or as a timeline.
